content:
inc-bot: INCIDENT P0 — GPU capacity exhausted in us-west1, autoscale failed (queue growing) <https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-20240614-01|INC-20240614-01>
chris: Paging oncall — we’re seeing sustained queue length + throttles for the realtime-generate route. 50% of requests now 503/timeout.
maya: Got the page, joining. Observability dashboard shows instance churn + multiple spot preemptions in last 18m.
raj: Confirming — autoscaler tried to spin up 4 nodes, two were preempted in provisioning window. Remaining capacity < min burst for our k8s-pool, so scale failed.
emily: Customer-facing impact: several customers on Dedicated and Hosted experiencing errors. Not yet SLA breach but error budget getting eaten. I’ll draft a customer advisory if we siren to SEs. :warning:
sre-rotations: Oncall summary — queue growth from 30 -> 120 req/s over 12m; average latency now 620ms; 95th token latency spiking. Throttling rate at 37%.
chris: Can we flip to fallback routing to CPU-quantized models for lower-priority tenants? We discussed degraded-mode policy but not used before.
maya: Trying to enable degraded routing to cpu-fallback policy for non-SLA routes now. Patch incoming: 
```bash
# enable degraded routing policy for route: realtime-generate
curl -X POST 'https://controlplane/api/routes/realtime-generate/override' -d '{"policy":"cpu-fallback","priority_threshold":0.5}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
```
chris: FYI that will increase latency but reduce error rate. Good trade for non-enterprise.
raj: Applying nodegroup resize to add reserved GPUs in us-west1, but we need approval for capacity commit. Provisioning request ticket created: CLOUD-REQ-4872.
cloud-support: We see high preemption rate for spot-gpu-pool-6 due to capacity reclaim. Recommend temporary switch to on-demand GPUs in region or try us-west2 capacity.
emily: Sales asked for list of impacted customers — I’ll compile and contact SEs. If this becomes multi-hour, we need a PR for credits.
sre-rotations: Quick mitigation steps executed:
- enabled degraded routing (non-SLA) -> drop 503 to 8% from 37% in 7m
- increased request timeout to 90s to avoid cascading retries
- disabled aggressive batching for short-context models to free VM slots
Results: queue length plateaued, throughput improved 22%.
maya: New problem — autoscaler hitting API rate limit on cloud provider when retrying spinups because of preemptions. We have 429s from cloud API.
chris: Oof. So autoscaler cannot create replacements; need manual intervention. Raj, can we manually create 2 reserved on-demand GPU instances and attach to pool?
raj: Starting manual spawn: `gcloud compute instances create ... --accelerator` — will attach to k8s node pool. ETA ~18m.
inc-bot: Note: Major incident declared by chris at 2024-06-14T10:07:00Z. Incident channel: #incidents.
sre-rotations: Observing that model-variant routing still tries to prefer high-perf quantized-gpu models; after enabling degraded routing we need to explicitly pin enterprise routes back.
chris: Emily — create a short customer advisory: what happened, who's impacted, mitigation steps, ETA for next update in 30m. Use template: "we experienced capacity exhaustion caused by spot GPU preemptions".
emily: Drafted advisory, posting to status page now.
```
Status update (EMERGENCY): We experienced capacity exhaustion in us-west1 due to spot GPU preemptions which caused autoscaling retries and queue growth. Mitigations: degraded routing to CPU models for non-SLA traffic; manual on-demand instance provisioning underway. Next update in 30m.
```
sales-ops: Any specific high-value customers affected? We have two enterprise customers on Dedicated in us-west1. Need direct outreach.
emily: Notified SEs and solutions for those two — SEs joining channel.
raj: Manual instance creation completed and nodes joined cluster. kubelet reports nodes Ready. Rolling pods to attach.
maya: After nodes Ready, we saw backlog drain slowly. Errors down to 4%. Latency still elevated.
chris: Good. Let's keep autoscaler off for this group until cloud-support confirms preemption risk reduced. Manual control only.
cloud-support: Confirmed broader capacity pressure in region for spot GPUs. On-demand availability limited but possible for small scale. Recommending multi-region fallback; us-west2 has spare capacity.
raj: Starting cross-region routing change for non-enterprise routes to prefer us-west2. Will update LB weights.
sre-rotations: Reminder: check token cache & KV caches after failover — we saw some cache misses leading to extra model warmups.
maya: Running cache warmup for top-10 models in us-west2 to reduce cold starts.
chris: Escalate to product — need default policy changes: avoid spinning spot preemptible-only pool for primary capacity for critical routes. We'll write a post-incident action.
emily: Customer advisory updated: additional note about credits for affected Dedicated customers if SLA impacted.
sre-rotations: Logging a postmortem ticket: PMORT-20240614-01. Action items so far:
- add preemption-aware autoscaler backoff and cloud API rate-limit resilience (owner: maya)
- FIFO queuing and early-degrade policy for spike control (owner: chris)
- automate fallback to reserve on-demand pool when preemption rate > X% (owner: raj)
- customer comms runbook updates (owner: emily)
chris: Thanks all. I'll remain here for handoff to night oncall in 45m. Maya, raj — drive the postmortem items.
maya: On it. Leaving a brief handoff to @sre-rotations for night.
sre-rotations: Handoff ack. I will monitor queue metrics and keep autoscaler disabled for the affected nodepool; contact cloud-support if preemptions resume.
inc-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: mitigations stable, traffic normalized to degraded route at 2024-06-14T12:20:00Z. Postmortem pending.
chris: Closing thread after postmortem created. Thanks everyone for quick response. :team-heart:
